title: Research Explained: 8,257 attacks on Europe - what ENISA's 2026 threat report found
description:
The EU Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA) analysed 8,257 cyber incidents from 2025 in its Threat Landscape 2026 report, published September 22, 2026. Here is what it found, where the data is thin, and what organisations should do this month.

Key findings (reporting period January 1 to December 31, 2025)
- DDoS was the most common incident type: 51.3% of incidents, mostly hacktivist campaigns with little large-scale impact.
- Financially motivated activity was 29.3% of incidents. Ransomware made up 47.3% of it, and ENISA calls it the most impactful threat in the short term.
- Where the entry route for unauthorised access was known, 60.4% exploited a vulnerability and 20.7% came from misconfiguration or accidental exposure.
- The limit: only 5.2% of those incidents had an identifiable entry route, so that figure rests on a thin slice of the data.
- Public administration was the most targeted sector: 31.8% of incidents, most of them DDoS.
- AI: attackers mostly used off-the-shelf AI tools to boost existing skills, not for breakthroughs. ENISA expects more attack stages to be directly AI-enabled in 2026.

Read with care
The report relies largely on public reporting, espionage often comes to light months or years later, and many attacker claims could not be verified. Some figures in ENISA's press release differ from the report; this video uses the report.

What to do this month (Securidge analysis)
1. Patch internet-facing systems first.
2. Check for misconfigured or exposed services.
3. Have a DDoS plan for public websites.
4. Keep offline backups and test a restore.

Sources
- ENISA Threat Landscape 2026 (report PDF): https://www.enisa.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2026-09/ENISA%20Threat%20Landscape%202026_Final.pdf
- ComplexDiscovery (Oct 2, 2026): https://complexdiscovery.com/enisa-threat-landscape-2026-finds-ddos-leads-incident-counts-while-ransomware-stays-most-impactful-in-the-short-term/

Narration uses an AI voice (ElevenLabs). Research, script and fact-check by Securidge.
